Amendment

/uh-MEND-ment/ · noun

Hear It

What It Means

Amendment means a minor change or addition made to a law, contract, or document, especially a constitution.

The senators spent the whole afternoon debating an amendment that would add stricter privacy language to the data bill.

Worked Example

The First Amendment to the U.S. Constitution added protections for speech, press, and religion to a document the states had already ratified.

The Constitution already existed as a finished text — the amendment is a formal change added to that existing document. An amendment never stands alone; it always modifies something already written.

Compare the words

Synonyms · words with a similar meaning

revision: a reworked version of an existing text

modification: a partial change to something

alteration: a change made to details

What it isn’t · antonyms and near-opposites

preservation: keeping something exactly as it is

retention: holding onto something unchanged

Where it sits · how sweeping the formal change is — tweak → amendment → overhaul

tweak vs. amendment: A tweak is milder than an amendment — the editor made a few informal tweaks to the wording without formally changing the contract at all.

overhaul vs. amendment: An overhaul is stronger than an amendment — rather than adjusting a few clauses, the committee proposed a complete overhaul that would rewrite the tax code from scratch.

Build the Word

The pieces

Prefix — a-

Prefix — a-: out of, away (from Latin e-/ex-, via Old French)

Root — mend

Root — mend: a fault, a flaw (Latin menda); to fix a fault

Suffix — -ment

Suffix — -ment: result or process of

Put it together

Put it together: Latin emendare meant "to free from fault" — e- (out) + menda (a fault). Filtered through Old French, it became amend. So an amendment is literally "the process of taking the faults out" of a text: you fix the document by changing its words.

Use the root in a new word: mend

Use the root in a new word: mend: After the argument, it took months for the two friends to mend — repair the faults in — their friendship.

Word Choice

Legal / civic

An amendment is an actual textual change to something already written — a constitution, a contract, a bill. Don't confuse it with a requirement: a requirement is a condition a person must meet; an amendment is a change made to the document itself. One new amendment can add or remove several requirements.
